canonical_definition: Visual Perception refers to the ability to perceive, extract, and interpret visual information from images or video, encompassing object recognition, identification of attributes (e.g., size, color, shape), understanding spatial and temporal relationships, and detection of patterns and semantic content. This capability serves as a foundational component for downstream multimodal reasoning, comprehension, and task execution (e.g., scene understanding, medical image analysis, forgery detection). Some definitions further emphasize technical aspects such as image encoding into visual tokens, OCR/icon detection, or the integration of lower-level perceptual sensitivity enhanced through multi-layer features, while others focus on higher-level tasks like action recognition, long-video scene interpretation, or puzzle-solving requiring structural awareness. Applications span general multimodal reasoning (e.g., VQA, captioning) and domain-specific contexts (e.g., UI navigation, medical imaging), reflecting variability in scope across papers.
